Fabricate

/FAB-ruh-kayt/ — stress on first syllable, rhymes with intricate · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To fabricate something is to invent or make it up in order to deceive people, such as fabricating false evidence or a fake excuse.

The student fabricated an elaborate excuse about a runaway parrot.

Worked Example

When caught without her ticket, she fabricated a detailed story about leaving it in her other bag, hoping the conductor would believe her.

Fabricate is more precise than 'lie' because it emphasizes actively CREATING or INVENTING something false, often with elaborate detail. A simple lie might deny an existing truth; fabrication is constructing an entire false narrative from scratch.

How Fabricate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

invent

invent: to make up something that never happened

lie

lie: to say something you know is false

concoct

concoct: to cook up an elaborate false story

Antonyms

verify

verify: to check and confirm something is true

confess

confess: to admit the truth you were hiding

How Strong Is It? — exaggerate → lie → fabricate → deceive

exaggerate vs. fabricate

exaggerate vs. fabricate: Exaggerate is weaker than fabricate; to exaggerate is to stretch a real fact bigger than it is, while to fabricate is to build a false one from nothing.

lie vs. fabricate

lie vs. fabricate: Lie is weaker than fabricate: a lie can be one quick false sentence, but to fabricate is to construct a whole detailed falsehood, piece by piece.

deceive vs. fabricate

deceive vs. fabricate: Deceive is stronger than fabricate — fabricating means manufacturing the false story itself, while deceiving is the larger act of making someone actually believe it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — fabric-

Root — fabric-: workshop; a craftsman's skillful making (Latin)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: to make or do (verb-forming) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: The root fabric- comes from Latin faber, 'craftsman,' and fabrica, 'workshop,' and -ate makes it a verb: 'to craft or construct.' To fabricate a story is to build it from scratch in the workshop of your imagination — manufacturing something false in order to deceive.

Use the root in a new word: prefabricated

Use the root in a new word: prefabricated: The prefabricated cabin was built in a factory workshop before being delivered — the same Latin 'workshop' root that lets fabricate mean constructing a story from scratch.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / neutral

Fabricate is the word when you want to emphasize actively MAKING UP an elaborate false story, not just denying one fact or telling a simple lie. For a basic untruth, 'lie' is more common. For creating something real, use 'build' or 'make.'
